brief: Goldman partner Bobby Molavi's Ruminations note argues traditional cross-asset correlations are broken and record equity highs coexist with a stress list still flashing red (Middle East escalation, sticky oil and diesel shortages, yields near multi-decade highs, pulled IPO issuance, rate-policy shifts, above-target inflation). His core claim: that stress list is not wrong, it has been demoted, because as long as belief in AI and AI capex holds, oil, rates, jobs, yields, and geopolitics stay secondary in how markets price risk, leaving index levels healthy only because they are narrow and concentrated in one theme (AI concentration near historic peaks seen in railroads, utilities and dot-com). This week's round-trip back to flat was driven by a dovish trifecta (soft jobs, tame PCE, G7 oil release) shifting odds toward a Fed pause, not structural resolution. Separately, US and UK 30-year yields hit multi-decade highs and French bonds had their worst quarter since the euro's creation, with the ECB politically constrained from intervening. October's auctions, earnings, elections and geopolitics will test whether the AI-driven referendum still clears.
